title: Belus
summary: Belus is dated in Raleigh's chronological table (1617), column Kings of Assyria , by a yeere of the World. No tier 1–4 chronology dates this person.
description: Added from the Raleigh import (The History of the World, 1617). Raleigh is display-only. He gives a yeere of the World, not a BC year, and no tier 1–4 chronology dates this person, so there is no sort year.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year. Raleigh is display-only and is not converted to BC.

death.date: He reigned sixty years, and died A. M. 1965
death.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book IV, p. 162 (facsimile PDF p. 258)
death.note: The sixty years are printed. A start year is not printed in this sentence. Page 172 places the beginning at A. M. 1905.

reign.citation: Raleigh, The History of the World (1617, EEBO-TCP A10357), Chronological Table, sig. 782a
reign.note: Year cell "2584 1902 245". The third printed figure 245 is the column "Floud", not a length. To the Reader (sig. 780b): the Julian Period exceeds the yeere of the World by 682. The 65 at the end of the name is the reign length he prints. The end year is not printed on this row. Column: Kings of Assyria ..

reign.date: “we have no certain tradition respecting the length of his reign”
reign.citation: Cory, Ancient Fragments (London: Reeves & Turner, 1876, ed. E. Richmond Hodges), p. 91; Castor, ap. Eusebius
reign.note: Castor commences the Assyrian canon with Belus and sets down the name only.

reign.date: he must begin his reign A. M. 1905
reign.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book IV, p. 172 (facsimile PDF p. 268)
reign.note: Shuckford’s conclusion against identifying Belus with Nimrod. The same page repeats the dispersion at A. M. 1757.
